'''Rosemary Gillespie''' is an [[evolutionary biologist]] and professor of Environmental Science, Policy & Management, Division of Insect Biology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rosemary G. Gillespie {{!}} Research UC Berkeley |url=https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/faculty/rosemary-g-gillespie |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=vcresearch.berkeley.edu}}</ref> She was the President of the [[American Genetic Association|American Genetics Association]] in 2018<ref>{{Cite web |title=AGA Officers & Council Members for 2017 |url=https://www.theaga.org/council.htm |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=www.theaga.org}}</ref> and was previously President of the International [[Biogeography]] Society 2013–2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=F. |first=Karen |title=Past Board Members |url=https://www.biogeography.org/about-us/board/past-board-members/ |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=[[International Biogeography Society]] |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2011 to 2013 she had served at the president of the [[American Arachnological Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AAS Governance: Officers, Directors, Committee Chairs |url=http://www.americanarachnology.org/governance/officers.html |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=www.americanarachnology.org |archive-date=December 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205025943/http://www.americanarachnology.org/governance/officers.html }}</ref> As of 2020 she is the faculty director of the [[Essig Museum of Entomology|Essig Museum]] of [[Entomology]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=People – Essig Museum of Entomology |url=https://essig.berkeley.edu/people/ |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=essig.berkeley.edu}}</ref> and a Professor and Schlinger Chair in systematic entomology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-01-20 |title=People |url=https://nature.berkeley.edu/evolab/people/ |access-date=2020-10-10 |website=Berkeley {{!}} Evolab |language=en-US}}</ref> Gillespie is known for her work on the evolution of communities on hotspot [[archipelago]]es.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gillespie |first1=Rosemary |title=Community assembly through adaptive radiation in Hawaiian spiders. |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |date=2004 |volume=303 |issue=5656 |pages=356–359 |doi=10.1126/science.1091875 |pmid=14726588 |bibcode=2004Sci...303..356G |s2cid=7748888}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gillespie |first1=Rosemary |last2=Roderick |first2=George |title=Arthropods on islands: colonization, speciation, and conservation. |journal=[[Annual Review of Entomology]] |date=2002 |volume=47 |issue=1 |pages=595–632 |doi=10.1146/annurev.ento.47.091201.145244 |pmid=11729086 |bibcode=2002AREnt..47..595G }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shaw |first1=Kerry L. |last2=Gillespie |first2=Rosemary G. |date=2016-07-19 |title=Comparative phylogeography of oceanic archipelagos: Hotspots for inferences of evolutionary process |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]] |language=en |volume=113 |issue=29|pages=7986–7993 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1601078113 |issn=0027-8424 |pmid=27432948 |pmc=4961166 |bibcode=2016PNAS..113.7986S |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Education and previous employment ==
She was born and raised in Scotland.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Kennedy |first1=Susan |last2=Krehenwinkel |first2=Henrik |date=2026 |title=Rosemary G. Gillespie—Recipient of the 2025 Molecular Ecology Prize |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/mec.70232 |journal=Molecular Ecology |language=en |volume=35 |issue=1 |article-number=e70232 |doi=10.1111/mec.70232 |bibcode=2026MolEc..3592423K |issn=1365-294X}}</ref> In 1980, she received her B.SC in [[zoology]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]], Scotland.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2014-06-01 |title=056: Dr. Rosemary Gillespie: Visualizing Evolutionary History of Spiders With Islands Providing Snapshots of Biodiversity |url=http://www.peoplebehindthescience.com/dr-rosemary-gillespie/ |access-date=2020-10-26 |website=People Behind the Science Podcast |language=en-US}}</ref> Gillespie moved to the United States to study the behavioral ecology of arachnids at the [[University of Tennessee]]-Knoxville where she earned her Ph.D.<ref name=":1" /> She then worked with the [[Sewanee: The University of the South|University of the South]], Sewanee, Tennessee.<ref name=":0" /> She went on to work as a postdoctoral researcher in 1987 at the [[University of Hawaii at Manoa|University of Hawaii]], working closely with The [[The Nature Conservancy|Nature Conservancy]] of Hawaii, based on the island of [[Maui]]. She took an appointment of Assistant Professor at the University of Hawaii at Manoa in 1992. She left Hawaii and moved to the University of California at Berkeley in 1999. As of 2002, Gillespie is the faculty director at the Department of Environmental Science, Policy and Management at UC Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rosemary GILLESPIE |url=https://ourenvironment.berkeley.edu/people/rosemary-gillespie |access-date=2020-10-26 |website=Our Environment at Berkeley |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
{{external media
| width = 250px
| float = right
| video1 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZFiO1QZHcaw "The World's Biota: Rosemary Gillespie"], October 4, 2017, [[University of California, Berkeley]]
| video2 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1_7WxVgJxbg&t=2s "Ecology, Evolution, and Species Diversification in Hawaiian Islands"], Rosemary Gillespie, June 7, 2016, [[Harvard Museum of Natural History]]
}}
Gillespie's research program is aimed at understanding what drives biological diversification, particularly at the level of populations and species.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gillespie |title=Island time & the interplay between ecology & evolution in species diversification |journal=[[Evolutionary Applications]] |date=2016 |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=53–73 |doi=10.1111/eva.12302 |doi-access=free |pmid=27087839 |pmc=4780372}}</ref> She uses islands of known age and isolation to assess the combined temporal and spatial dimension of biogeography and determine patterns of diversification, adaptive radiation, and associated community assembly with a focus on spiders and insects.<ref name=":1" /> Most of her work has been in the [[Hawaiian Islands]], though she has also worked in [[French Polynesia]], [[Fiji]], [[Pohnpei]], and [[Kosrae]]. Themes include adaptive radiation and community assembly on islands with emphasis on patterns of repeated [[evolution]] of similar forms, the rate of species accumulation and approach to equilibrium within an island system, and mechanisms of dispersal to the islands.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gillespie |first1=Rosemary |last2=Baldwin |first2=Bruce |last3=Waters |first3=Jonathan |last4=Fraser |first4=Ceridwen |last5=Nikula |first5=R. |last6=Roderick |first6=George |title=Long-distance dispersal-a framework for hypothesis testing |journal=[[Trends in Ecology & Evolution]] |date=2012 |volume=27 |issue=1 |pages=52–61 |doi=10.1016/j.tree.2011.08.009 |pmid=22014977 |bibcode=2012TEcoE..27...52G }}</ref> Most of her work has been on spiders, in particular species in the genus [[Tetragnatha]] (Tetragnathidae). She also works on the evolution of diversity within species, with the primary focus here on color polymorphism in the [[Theridion grallator|Hawaiian Happy face spider]] which has evolved the same color [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphism]] independently on different islands, and the research aims to uncover the molecular basis for the modification.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Croucher |first1=Peter |last2=Oxford |first2=Geoff |last3=Lam |first3=Athena |last4=Mody |first4=N. |last5=Gillespie |first5=Rosemary |title=Colonization history and population genetics of the exuberantly color polymorphic Hawaiian happy-face spider Theridion grallator (Araneae, Theridiidae) |journal=[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]] |date=2012 |volume=66 |issue=9 |pages=2815–2833 |doi=10.1111/j.1558-5646.2012.01653.x |pmid=22946805 |doi-access=free}}</ref> She currently has a large program examining the importance of priority, sequence, abundance, and interaction strengths in determining how biological communities develop,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rominger |first1=Andrew |last2=Goodman |first2=Kari |last3=Lim |first3=Jun Ying |last4=Valdovinos |first4=Fernanda |last5=Price |first5=Donald |last6=Percy |first6=Diana |last7=Roderick |first7=George |last8=Shaw |first8=Kerry |last9=Gruner |first9=Daniel |last10=Gillespie |first10=Rosemary |title=Community assembly on isolated islands: Macroecology meets evolution |journal=[[Global Ecology and Biogeography]] |date=2016 |volume=25 |issue=7 |pages=769–780 |doi=10.1111/geb.12341 |bibcode=2016GloEB..25..769R |url=http://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/9fg952km|hdl=10342/10095 |s2cid=17654773 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and how this might render them resilient to intrusion by non-native species.

== Science communication ==
Gillespie led "Exploring California Biodiversity" (2003-2016), a [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF)-funded museum and field-based outreach program focused on graduate fellows and high-school/middle-school students in minority-dominated urban schools in the Bay Area.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0231877 |title=NSF Award Search: Award#0231877 - GK-12: Exploring California Biodiversity |website=www.nsf.gov |access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> The project forged connections between the university and the surrounding community, enriching K-12 science education, and training graduate students to be better communicators of science. Prior to moving to UC Berkeley she was part of an effort for Using Hawaii's Unique Biota for Biology Education, an NSF program that worked with underrepresented Pacific Island students.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=9979656 |title=NSF Award Search: Award#9979656 - Using Hawaii's Unique Biota for Biology Education in a GK-12 Project |website=www.nsf.gov |access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> She also led or co-led several programs to encourage participation of underrepresented minorities in higher education, including an NSF-funded Undergraduate Mentoring in Environmental Biology program that encouraged Pacific Islander undergraduates to undertake field and laboratory research in biology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aibs.org/eye-on-education/eye_on_education_2004_01.html |title=AIBS Eye on Education {{!}} Undergraduate Mentoring Program Targets Hard-to-Find Students |website=www.aibs.org |access-date=2019-12-05 |archive-date=December 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205024456/https://www.aibs.org/eye-on-education/eye_on_education_2004_01.html }}</ref> She was awarded NSF's [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring]] (PAESMEM) in Nov 2005.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://nature.berkeley.edu/news/2005/11/rosemary-gillespie-receives-presidential-award-excellence-mentoring |title=Rosemary Gillespie receives Presidential Award for Excellence in Mentoring |website=[[UC Berkeley College of Natural Resources]] |language=en |access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> In 2026, Gillespie was awarded the 2025 Molecular Ecology Prize.<ref name=":1" />
